data.standardized_narrative: Syndicate 1910 opened 2023 with gross claims outstanding of GBP 792.7m. The syndicate reports an improvement in prior year reserves for 2022 and 2021 driven by favourable claims experience in longer-tail and specialty classes; however no single aggregate gross prior-year development figure is provided in the notes (RITC and portfolio movements distort direct comparators). Several named catastrophe events from prior years (e.g. Hurricane Ida, Winter Storm Uri, European and Australian floods, and the Ukraine conflict) are referenced as drivers of prior loss activity. The claims development table is provided by underwriting year but is affected by reinsurance-to-close adjustments, so a reliable single gross prior year movement amount cannot be unambiguously derived from the published data.
raw_causal_phrases: The Syndicate has also seen improvement in its prior year reserves for 2022 & 2021, due to good experience on its longer tail and specialty classes.
There was limited landfall in populated areas leading to a much-improved syndicate result in 2023 for the current year of account.

2023 did see a material impact from convective storms in the US, totalling more than $50bn, according to PCS Catastrophe Loss Index. However, increased retentions and a reduction in aggregate exposure (On convective storm exposed policies) in the Syndicate portfolio saw the incurred losses from this peril reduce year on year.
